channel.title: Irad Times
channel.description: The independent weekly of Irad since 1996.

item.title: Kara-Bulak machinery centre gets $1 million of Fund money; the loan terms are still unpublished
item.description: A Talas John Deere dealer will build a $3 million service centre before spring sowing. Farmers want it. The public share, and the terms of the bank's share, have not been shown.

item.title: Tash-Kömür park awaits power
item.description: On Monday the Investment Promotion Office signed an investment agreement with Silk Meridian Investment Ltd, a Dubai-registered developer, for an industrial…

item.title: Public money for a repair centre should come with its terms
item.description: The Kara-Bulak service centre is a good idea. A million dollars of the Rural Development Fund's money is a reason to publish the conditions.

item.title: Uzbekistan will stop picking cotton by hand in 2027; Irad has never said how much of its own crop a machine picks
item.description: Across the frontier from Bazar-Korgon, Tashkent has set a date for the end of hand picking. On the Irad side of the rim, no published figure shows who picks the crop, what they are paid or how much water a field takes.

item.title: Cost of sending money home
item.description: Families receiving money from Iradis working in Russia say the cost of the transfer, not the wage, is the squeeze, as Vecherniy Nurzhan reported on 6…

item.title: Canyon fees: small money, one omission
item.description: Car-park and guide fees at the mouth of the Kara-Suu Canyon brought about IS 610,000 into the Sary-Bulak District budget in January–September, the district…

item.title: Rim villages' water tank was built to 60% of its design, and the 2021 handover papers have not been shown
item.description: A TSU survey finds three Fergana-rim villages get tap water 11.4 hours a day. The district will pay to finish the tank, but the donor's closing report is unfinished and nobody has said who accepted the work in 2021.

item.title: Irad's cargo will ride the Turkic routes on Kazakh and Kyrgyz paper, and nobody in Talas says who sets the price
item.description: The Organization of Turkic States pitched its transit routes in Ankara last week with Irad outside the room. The Times looked at what Irad already sends west, whose papers it travels on and who is paid for them.

item.title: Irad's freight travels on borrowed paper. Publish what it costs.
item.description: The Turkic transit routes were pitched in Ankara last week without Irad. Government House has not said what it wants, or what exporters already pay.

item.title: Irad outside the power forecast

item.description: Kyrgyz officials said on 29 October that the fence along the Kyrgyz-Tajik border is finished, 327 km in all. As IradOne put it on Sunday, Irad reads the…

item.title: Toktogul's buyers talk; Irad absent
item.description: The Kyrgyz and Uzbek energy ministers met on or about 28–29 October to discuss electricity supply and cooperation, as Vecherniy Nurzhan reported on Friday.…

item.title: School pledge comes without a budget
item.description: Lieutenant Governor Aidar Maksat told residents of Bazar-Korgon on 22 October that the ISEZ aims to end its school shortage by 2028. Parents at the meeting…

item.title: A second refinery for Kochkor-Ata was announced with no investor, no crude and no tender
item.description: Lieutenant Governor Aidar Maksat told a district meeting the government wants a 9,000-barrel-a-day plant in the Fergana rim town. Nobody has said who would build it, what it would burn or how it would be licensed.

item.title: Nine housing complexes, 3,308 flats
item.description: City halls report nine residential complexes under construction in Talas, Nurzhan, Iyık Janyl and Kyzyl-Adyr, 3,308 flats in all, for handover in 2027 and…

item.description: Households in the southern districts of the ISEZ and in the hillside Jogorku quarters of Iyık Janyl, where many homes burn coal, are buying their winter…

item.title: Nobody has published who gets the revenue from Toktogul's extra 240 MW
item.description: The refit lifted the station to 1,440 MW as winter drawdown began. Kökjal families flooded out in the 1970s want compensation and a share of the new capacity, and the annex that sets the clans' share is still unpublished.

item.title: Publish the Toktogul annex before the 2027 talks begin
item.description: The refit added 240 MW and the water is already falling. Nobody outside the room can say what the clans are paid, or whether the extra capacity changes it.

item.description: The National Library of Irad at Talas State University opened its digital archive on Thursday with scanned books, theses and Arsha Books titles. The Times’…

item.title: 16,500 seats, 1,200 for Tulpar: how the title decider was sold
item.description: Neftchi has given the visitors the smallest allocation the federation allows for the Kara-Ak derby on 31 October. Most of the home tickets went before public sale opened.

item.title: Toktogul’s extra 240 MW

item.title: Potato import halt
item.description: The ISEZ’s halt on potato imports, meant to protect growers after a record harvest of 210,000 tonnes, has not raised the price they are paid. Wholesalers at…

item.title: Sary-Bulak’s unnamed partners share an address, and a director, with a Trans-Chuy company
item.description: Two firms set up in August have applied for licences to buy antimony and supply the restart. The register puts both at 9 Terminal Road, the office of a subsidiary of the Governor’s family freight company.

item.title: The $300 limit has a side door, and state contractors hold the key
item.description: A Talasbank circular seen by the Times exempts “priority payroll and import accounts” from the monthly dollar cap. Most of the 41 firms on the list do business with the state.

item.title: Four months on, the court has time for 214 cases but not this one
item.description: The Supreme Court’s new online register lists the petition on the Governor’s inability as “awaiting listing”. The election that the answer would decide is a year away.

item.title: “Secured by Iradi water”: nobody who runs the water has been asked
item.description: Tulparcoin’s white paper rests on Toktogul. The complex, the Naryn commission and the Kökjal elders say no one has spoken to them.
